title: There was a time when you were not even mentioned.
subtitle: Before you existed
then: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this surah in the Friday dawn prayer, as Ibn Abbas reported in Sahih Muslim. Ibn Kathir says Allah brought man into being {trap}after he was not even a thing worth mentioning, because of his lowliness and weakness.{/trap} {idea}The surah opens with a question you can only answer yes.{/idea}
now: Your name is on your ID, your email, your work badge. People tag you in photos. It feels like you have always been someone. {idea}A short while ago, no one on earth could have said your name.{/idea}
old: I have always been here, and I am owed my place.
new: I was nothing worth mentioning, then Allah mentioned me into being.
try: Say Alhamdulillah for simply existing, once, slowly, before you sleep.

title: Made from a mixed drop, given ears and eyes, to be tested.
subtitle: Why you were given hearing and sight
then: Ibn Abbas said the mixed drop is {idea}the fluid of the man and the woman when they meet and mix{/idea}, then man changes stage to stage. Ibn Kathir says hearing and sight were given {trap}so he could use them for obedience or disobedience.{/trap}
now: Your earbuds are in all day. Your eyes are on a screen for hours. Those are the two gifts this verse names. {idea}Every song, every clip, every page is part of an exam you did not notice you were sitting.{/idea}
old: My eyes and ears are mine to use however I want.
new: My eyes and ears were given for a test. What I feed them is my answer.
try: Choose one thing to listen to or watch today that you would want counted for you.

title: The way was shown. Grateful or ungrateful is your part.
subtitle: Guidance given, choice left open
then: Ibn Kathir says "We guided him" means {idea}We explained it, made it clear, and showed it to him{/idea}: the path of good and the path of evil. He cites the hadith: {trap}every person wakes up as a merchant of his own soul, either ruining it or setting it free.{/trap}
now: Your alarm rings. Before you open your eyes, the day is already a market. How you speak to your kids, what you do with your lunch hour, what you say about a coworker. {idea}Each one is a small trade with your own soul.{/idea}
old: I never really got a clear picture of what is right.
new: The way has been shown. Today I choose gratitude or not.
try: When you wake tomorrow, say one line of thanks before you touch your phone.

title: For the ungrateful path, chains and a blaze.
subtitle: One end of the fork, named briefly
then: Having said man is either grateful or ungrateful, the surah names the end of the second path in one verse. Ibn Kathir says {trap}Sa'ir is the flame and fire of Hell.{/trap} Then, at once, {idea}the surah spends many verses on the righteous.{/idea}
now: You tell yourself no one can chain you: you do what you want, when you want. But the late-night habit, the temper, the debt you keep feeding already feel heavy. {idea}Ingratitude starts as freedom and ends as chains.{/idea}
old: Living without limits is real freedom.
new: Turning from Allah ends in chains. Gratitude is the real freedom.
try: Name one habit that already feels like a chain, and loosen it one notch today.

title: The righteous drink a cup mixed with camphor.
subtitle: Cool, fragrant, delicious

key.label: The other end of the fork

then: Right after the blaze comes a cool drink. Ibn Kathir says camphor is known for being {reward}cooling and fragrant, and in Paradise its taste will be delicious.{/reward} The contrast is deliberate: {idea}fire for one path, coolness for the other.{/idea}
now: A long fasting day in summer. The first sip of cold water at sunset. Nothing in the world tastes better. {reward}That is a hint of what this verse promises.{/reward}
old: Doing right is all effort and no taste.
new: The righteous path ends in a sweetness I can barely imagine.
try: With your next cold drink, say Bismillah and remember this cup.

title: A spring they direct wherever they wish.
subtitle: Abundance under their control
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's close servants {reward}drink from it directly, to their fill.{/reward} Mujahid said {idea}they will divert it wherever they wish{/idea}: to their castles, homes, and sitting rooms.
now: The water bill. The tap that runs slow in summer. The bottle you carry because you are never sure. {reward}This verse describes water that never runs out and goes where you send it.{/reward}
old: Good things are always scarce and I have to fight for them.
new: For Allah's servants, there is a spring that never runs short.
try: Give someone water today, a glass, a bottle, a donation to a well.

title: They keep their promises and fear a spreading Day.
subtitle: The first trait of the righteous
then: Ibn Kathir says they worship Allah with what is required and {idea}also by fulfilling what they vowed.{/idea} Qatadah said the evil of that Day {trap}will spread until it fills the heavens and the earth.{/trap} Their fear of it shapes what they do now.
now: You said "if this works out, I will give to charity." It worked out. Weeks passed. {idea}The righteous are the ones who remember what they promised Allah when things got better.{/idea}
old: A promise to Allah made in a hard moment can be forgotten later.
new: Keeping my word to Allah, even a small one, marks the righteous.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah and do part of it today.

title: They give away food they themselves want.
subtitle: Feeding the poor, the orphan, the captive
then: Mujahid said they give food {idea}while they themselves love it and desire it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {reward}the best charity is given while you are healthy and stingy, hoping to be rich and fearing poverty.{/reward} The captive, some said, included non-Muslim prisoners.
now: You bought the good dates for yourself. Someone at the door, or a neighbor having a hard month, comes to mind. Giving the cheap box is easy. {reward}Giving the one you were looking forward to is the verse.{/reward}
old: I give once I have more than enough.
new: The giving that counts most is the giving that costs me something I want.
try: Give away one thing today that you actually like, food, a meal, your time.

title: We want no payback, not even a thank you.
subtitle: Giving for Allah's Face alone
then: Ibn Kathir says they seek no reward and {trap}do not want to be thanked in front of people.{/trap} Mujahid and Sa'id bin Jubayr said: {idea}they did not say this with their tongues. Allah knew it in their hearts and praised them for it.{/idea}
now: You helped your friend move all Saturday. They did not say thanks. It stings for days. {idea}This verse asks: who did you do it for?{/idea}
old: If no one thanks me, my good deed was wasted.
new: When I give for Allah, a missing thank you takes nothing away.
try: Do one kind thing today and tell no one about it.

title: Their giving is shaped by fear of a frowning Day.
subtitle: The hard, long Day they prepare for
then: Ibn Kathir says they do it {idea}so that perhaps Allah will have mercy on them on that Day.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said 'abus means {trap}difficult{/trap} and qamtarir means {trap}long.{/trap} Others said faces will frown and foreheads tighten from dismay.
now: You worry at night about death, about the Day, about whether you are good enough. The worry just sits there. {idea}These people turned the same worry into a plate of food for someone hungry.{/idea}
old: Fearing the Day just makes me anxious.
new: Fear of the Day can become a reason to be kind today.
try: Next time you feel that fear, turn it into one act of giving.

title: Saved from the Day they feared, given light and joy.
subtitle: Radiant faces, happy hearts
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}protected them from what they feared{/reward} and gave them {reward}radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts.{/reward} He notes that a happy heart lights the face, as Ka'b bin Malik described the Prophet's ﷺ face shining like a piece of the moon when he was happy.
now: You have seen it: the face of someone who just gave something big away. A mother after feeding a crowd. {idea}Joy inside shows on the outside.{/idea} The Day will show it fully.
old: Giving things away leaves me with less.
new: What I give for Allah comes back as light in my face and joy in my heart.
try: Notice how you feel after the next thing you give. Thank Allah for it.

title: Their reward is because they were patient.
subtitle: Patience in leaving their desires
then: Ibn Kathir says because of their patience Allah gives them {reward}a spacious home, a delightful life, and fine clothing.{/reward} When this verse was recited to Abu Sulayman Ad-Darani, he said: {idea}because they were patient in leaving off their desires in the world.{/idea}
now: You wanted the expensive thing and bought the plain one so you could give. You wanted to sleep and stood up to pray. {idea}Nobody saw it as patience. Allah did.{/idea}
old: Saying no to what I want is just loss.
new: Every desire I leave for Allah is patience, and patience is paid.
try: Say no to one small desire today, and give it to Allah.

title: No burning sun, no biting cold.
subtitle: Rest in a climate that never troubles
then: Ibn Kathir says there will be {reward}no disturbing heat and no painful cold, only one climate, always{/reward}, and they will not want it changed. Earlier, the righteous were patient. {idea}Now they recline.{/idea}
now: You check the weather app every morning. Too hot to walk, too cold to go out, the AC bill, the heating bill. {reward}A place where the weather is never a problem is part of the promise.{/reward}
old: Discomfort is just a permanent part of life.
new: Every hot or freezing day here can be borne with a place of rest in mind.
try: Next time the weather annoys you, say: there is a Garden with none of this.

title: Shade close by, fruit that bends down to you.
subtitle: Nothing out of reach
then: Mujahid said {reward}if he stands it rises with him, if he sits it lowers, if he lies down it lowers more.{/reward} Qatadah said {idea}no thorn or distance keeps their hands from it.{/idea}
now: Everything good here seems just out of reach: the promotion, the house, the rest you need. You keep stretching. {reward}In the Garden, what you want comes to you.{/reward}
old: Everything I want, I have to reach and strain for.
new: There is a place where good things bend toward me.
try: Share fruit with someone today, and remember the fruit that bends down.

title: Silver vessels and cups passed around to them.
subtitle: Served, not serving
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}servants will go around them with silver vessels of food and cups of drink.{/reward} These are the same people who, a few verses earlier, {idea}fed the poor, the orphan, and the captive while wanting the food themselves.{/idea}
now: You are the one who always serves: the tea at family gatherings, the plates after Eid dinner, the one who clears the table. {reward}One day the plates come to you.{/reward}
old: Being the one who serves means I am at the bottom.
new: Those who served others here will be served there.
try: Serve someone at your table today before you serve yourself.

title: Silver as clear as glass, filled just right.
subtitle: Measured to your exact thirst
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it is {reward}the whiteness of silver in the transparency of glass{/reward}, something with no likeness in this world. The measure is {idea}exactly what quenches their thirst, not more, not less.{/idea}
now: You pour too much and waste it. You order too little and leave hungry. Nothing here is ever quite right. {reward}The Garden is precise to your need.{/reward}
old: Nothing in life ever fits me exactly.
new: Allah knows my measure. In the Garden it is met exactly.
try: Take only as much as you need at your next meal.

title: A cup mixed with ginger, warm after the cool.
subtitle: Balance in every delight
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}one time they are given a drink mixed with camphor, which is cool, and another time with ginger, which is warm{/reward}, so their state is balanced. Those nearest to Allah {idea}drink from all of it as they wish.{/idea}
now: Ginger tea on a cold evening, a cold drink at noon. Your body needs both. {reward}The Garden is not just more. It is perfectly balanced.{/reward}
old: Paradise sounds like the same pleasure over and over.
new: The Garden is full of variety and balance, designed with care.
try: Make a cup of something warm today and thank Allah for its taste.

title: A spring there named Salsabil.
subtitle: A spring that never stops flowing
then: Ikrimah said {reward}Salsabil is the name of a spring in Paradise.{/reward} Mujahid said it is called this {idea}because of its continuous flowing and the strength of its current.{/idea}
now: You saved your energy for a weekend that went too fast. Joy here comes in drips: a good day, a good meal, then it is over. {reward}This spring is named for never stopping.{/reward}
old: Good times always run out.
new: There is a joy that keeps flowing and never runs dry.
try: When a good moment ends today, ask Allah for the joy that does not end.

title: Servants like scattered pearls, forever young.
subtitle: The beauty of those who serve them
then: Ibn Kathir says they stay {reward}in one state forever, never growing older.{/reward} Seeing them rush to serve, with their beauty and fine clothes, {idea}you would think them scattered pearls{/idea}, and nothing is lovelier than pearls in a beautiful place.
now: You notice your first grey hairs in the bathroom mirror. Your kids grow, your parents slow down. {reward}The Garden is a place where time stops taking.{/reward}
old: Losing youth and beauty is just how it is.
new: Nothing in the Garden fades. What is lost here is not lost forever.
try: Use one hour of your health today for something that lasts.

title: Look there, and you see delight and a great kingdom.
subtitle: Even the least of them gets ten worlds
then: Ibn Kathir cites the authentic hadith: Allah will tell {idea}the last person to leave the Fire and enter Paradise{/idea}, {reward}you have the like of the world and ten times more.{/reward} If that is the least, he asks, what of those higher than him?
now: You compare your flat to your cousin's house, your salary to your friend's. The world feels like a race for a bigger slice. {reward}The smallest place in the Garden is bigger than the whole world, ten times over.{/reward}
old: I need more of this world to be satisfied.
new: The smallest share there is more than all of this world.
try: The next time you feel envy today, remember the ten worlds.

title: Their Lord gives them a drink that purifies.
subtitle: Beautiful outside, clean inside
then: Ibn Kathir says the drink {reward}purifies their insides of envy, hatred, harm, and every bad trait.{/reward} Ali bin Abi Talib said at the gate of Paradise they will drink from one spring and {idea}Allah will remove whatever harm is inside them.{/idea}
now: You dress well for the wedding and smile at the cousin you secretly resent. The outside is fine. Inside is a knot. {reward}In the Garden there is no knot left.{/reward}
old: Looking good is enough.
new: Allah cares about a clean heart, and in the Garden He makes it fully clean.
try: Make dua today for someone you feel envy toward.

title: This is your reward. Your effort has been appreciated.
subtitle: Small deeds, large return
then: Ibn Kathir says this will be said {reward}to honor them.{/reward} Allah {idea}rewards a small amount of deeds with a large amount of reward.{/idea} The people who wanted no thanks from anyone in verse 9 are thanked by Allah.
now: You cleaned up after everyone and no one noticed. You stayed up with a sick child and no one knew. {reward}One day you will hear: your effort was appreciated.{/reward}
old: If no one notices my effort, it does not count.
new: Allah notices every effort and repays it far more than it was.
try: Keep going with one unseen effort today, knowing it is seen.

title: We sent the Quran down to you, piece by piece.
subtitle: A reminder of the honor first
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}reminds His Messenger ﷺ of how He blessed him by revealing the Quran.{/reward} The next verse asks for patience. {idea}The blessing is named before the burden.{/idea}
now: A hard week: a deadline, a fight at home, money short. You forget everything good. {idea}Before asking for patience, Allah reminds you what you have been given.{/idea} You have the Quran in your pocket.
old: My troubles are the main story of my life.
new: I have been honored with guidance. That comes first, then the patience.
try: Read one short passage of the Quran today as a gift, not a task.

title: Be patient with His decree. Do not obey those pulling you away.
subtitle: Patience and refusing pressure
then: Ibn Kathir says: {reward}be patient with His decree and know He will handle your affairs well.{/reward} Do not obey those who {trap}want to turn you from what was revealed to you.{/trap} The sinner is wrong in his deeds; the denier is wrong in his heart.
now: Your friends make fun of your prayer breaks. A coworker says you are too strict. The pressure is gentle but constant. {idea}Patience here means not bending, and trusting Allah with the result.{/idea}
old: If enough people push me, it is fine to give in a little.
new: I can be patient and still not obey those pulling me from what is right.
try: Hold one small line today that you usually give up under pressure.

title: Remember your Lord's name, morning and evening.
subtitle: How patience is fueled
then: Right after being told to be patient and not give in, the Prophet ﷺ is told {idea}to remember his Lord's name at the beginning of the day and at its end.{/idea} {reward}That is where patience is refilled.{/reward}
now: Your morning starts with a phone full of notifications, and ends the same way. {idea}Put Allah's name at both ends instead.{/idea} A short dhikr before the phone, and one after it is off.
old: I will stay patient by gritting my teeth.
new: Patience is fed by remembering Allah at the start and end of my day.
try: Tomorrow morning, say one dhikr before you check your phone.

title: And at night, prostrate and glorify Him long.
subtitle: The night as a place of strength
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the command in Surah Al-Isra to {idea}pray at night as an extra prayer{/idea}, and to the opening of Al-Muzzammil: {reward}stand the night, except a little.{/reward} The night is where the Prophet ﷺ gathered strength for the day.
now: Midnight, the house is silent, and you are on your phone again. Ten minutes of that could be two rakahs. {idea}No one sees you. That is the point.{/idea}
old: The night is just for sleep or downtime.
new: Some of the night is a private meeting with Allah that gives me strength.
try: Before sleep tonight, pray two short rakahs, even just two.

title: They love the now and leave a heavy Day behind them.
subtitle: Why people turn away
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}reproaches those who love the world, devoted to it, who put the Hereafter behind them.{/trap} The heavy Day is {idea}the Day of Judgement.{/idea} This explains the pressure in verse 24.
now: You put the hard letter in a drawer so you do not have to see it. It is still there. The deadline still comes. {idea}Putting the Day behind you does not make it lighter.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about the Day, it will not weigh on me.
new: The Day is heavy whether I look at it or not. Better to face it.
try: Spend two minutes today thinking honestly about the Day, then do one good thing.

title: We made you strong, and We can remake you.
subtitle: Your strength is His creation
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said it means {idea}their creation.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the second half means {idea}We will resurrect them and repeat their creation{/idea}; Ibn Jarir said it also means {trap}Allah could bring another people in their place.{/trap}
now: You are proud of your gym routine, your sharp mind, your health. It feels self-made. {idea}The frame you are proud of was built by Him and can be rebuilt by Him.{/idea}
old: My strength is something I made myself.
new: My strength was given. The One who gave it can replace me, or raise me again.
try: Use your strength today to help someone weaker, carry something, lift something.

title: This is a reminder. Whoever wills, take a path to your Lord.
subtitle: The door is open
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this surah is a reminder{/idea}, and the path is {reward}for whoever wants to be guided by the Quran.{/reward} He compares it to the verse: what loss would they have if they believed?
now: You feel you are too far gone, too many years of not praying, too many mistakes. {reward}The verse does not list requirements. It says: whoever wills.{/reward}
old: The path to Allah is for people better than me.
new: The path is open to anyone who wants it, including me.
try: Take one step on the path today: one prayer, one page, one sincere dua.

title: You cannot will unless Allah wills.
subtitle: Even the wanting is from Him
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}no one can guide himself, enter faith, or benefit himself unless Allah wills.{/idea} He knows who deserves guidance and {reward}makes it easy for him.{/reward}
now: You finally started praying regularly and feel quietly proud. Or you keep trying and failing and feel hopeless. {idea}Both feelings forget something: the will to turn is itself a gift from Allah.{/idea} So ask Him for it.
old: Staying on the path is all down to my own effort.
new: My effort matters, but it rests on Allah's will. I ask Him to keep me.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to keep your heart firm on His path.

title: He admits whom He wills into His mercy.
subtitle: The surah ends where it began: two paths
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}whoever He guides, no one can lead astray; whoever He leaves astray, no one can guide.{/idea} The surah opened with two paths, grateful or ungrateful, and closes with their two ends: {reward}His mercy{/reward} or {trap}a painful punishment for wrongdoers.{/trap}
now: You finish this surah on a Friday morning, maybe in the dawn prayer. Two paths, two ends, laid out start to finish. {reward}The door to His mercy is the one this surah keeps pointing to.{/reward}
old: I will figure out which way I am going later.
new: There are two ends. I ask Allah, today, to admit me into His mercy.
try: Ask Allah, by name, to enter you into His mercy, in your own words.
